title: Pecan pie
subtitle: American pecan pie with a dark brown sugar filling
excerpt: Pecan pie is a blind-baked shortcrust case filled with a mixture of melted butter, brown sugar, golden syrup, eggs, and pecan halves. You get a filling that sets to a firm, fudgy texture with a crisp pecan layer on top. Watch the fill level: too full and the custard overflows during baking; too short and the ratio of pastry to filling is wrong.
sourceNotes: Pecan pie is an American Southern classic, with recipes appearing in regional cookery collections from the late 19th century. The standard filling uses corn syrup in American versions; this recipe uses golden syrup, which is the most widely available substitute in the UK and gives a comparable result. The method follows the standard approach documented in home-baking literature on both sides of the Atlantic.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked and cooled pie, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and bring to room temperature before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pie can be baked the day before. Keep at room temperature, covered. Serve at room temperature.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 180 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 165 degrees Celsius. Middle shelf. The filling needs gentle, even heat to set without the nuts burning.

glossaryTerms.definition: Baking an unfilled pastry case so the crust sets before any wet filling goes in. The case is lined with baking paper and weighted with ceramic beans or dried pulses so the base stays flat and the sides do not slump.

A pastry made by rubbing cold fat into flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs, then binding with the minimum amount of cold water. The fat limits gluten development, giving a crumbly, tender result.

content.text: before a syrup, sugar, and egg filling is poured in. The pecans float to the surface during baking and form the characteristic crunchy top layer. The filling sets similarly to a soft caramel: firm enough to slice but not dry. The most common mistake is pulling the pie too early; the centre should only barely wobble.
Making the pastry and blind baking

Rub the cold cubed butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture looks like rough breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and cold water a tablespoon at a time, cutting through with a knife, until the dough just comes together. Press into a disc, wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius conventional. Roll the chilled pastry to a circle about 3 mm thick. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, trim the overhang, and prick the base. Line with crumpled baking paper, fill with baking beans, and blind bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 5 minutes until the base is dry and pale gold. Remove from the oven. Keep the oven at 180 degrees Celsius.
Melt the 100 g of butter for the filling in a small saucepan over low heat. Add the soft brown sugar and stir until dissolved and the mixture looks smooth. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the golden syrup, then the 3 beaten eggs, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Mix until combined. Add the pecan halves and stir through.

Set the blind-baked tart tin on a baking tray. Pour the pecan filling into the warm case. The pecans will settle unevenly; arrange any that are on their sides so the flat side faces up for a neater finish.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the filling is set at the edges and only slightly wobbly at the very centre. The surface will be deep amber and the pecans will look toasted and dry rather than wet. A skewer inserted 3 cm from the edge should come out with just a few sticky crumbs, not liquid.
Leave the pie to cool in the tin on a rack for at least 20 minutes before releasing. The filling continues to firm as it cools and is best sliced at room temperature.

items.symptom: Filling is still liquid after cooling
items.cause: Underbaked, or the egg ratio was off.
items.fix: The filling should only wobble very slightly at the centre when it comes out of the oven. If it moves freely, give it another 5 to 10 minutes, covering the edges with foil if the pastry has already coloured.
items.avoid: Avoid pulling the pie while the centre still moves like water.

items.symptom: Pecan surface is very dark before the filling sets
items.cause: Oven too hot or top shelf position.
items.fix: Lay a sheet of foil loosely over the top for the last 10 to 15 minutes of baking. The filling will continue to set without the surface burning.
items.avoid: Avoid placing the pie higher than the middle shelf.

items.cause: Blind bake was too short, or the base was not fully dry before the filling went in.
items.fix: The 5-minute uncovered bake after removing the beans is not optional. The base should look dry and feel set, not soft, when you touch it.
items.avoid: Avoid filling the case immediately after removing the beans without the uncovered bake.
